title: The end of the year
steps: That voice in the walls has a name: Korvel.
He was, like you, a pupil of this school. And, later, a teacher.
Many years ago, he wrote enchantments on the castle itself.
At first he did it to make it better: safer, more comfortable, more magical.
But little by little he slipped in changes, small touches to the spells…
…so that the castle would obey him alone.
Other wizards and I saw what he was doing, and we drove him out.
Your parents, {wizard}, are not what you think. They both studied here, and they too were pupils of mine.
They were wizards, and among the best. They set about rewriting the castle's spells…
…they kept the good, so that it would go on teaching the new pupils every year and protecting wizards…
…and took out what Korvel had put in to control it.
Korvel came back to kill them. But your mother was already carrying you…
…and you, not yet born, protected them both.
Korvel could kill only the magic in them.
That is why they are not wizards now, and why they remember nothing.
The spells they had written were not yet finished, nor tied off.
When your parents' magic died they came undone, and the castle's magic fell with them.
That killed Korvel too: greedy for power, and seeking to live for ever…
…he had put all his magic, his own soul, into those spells.
It took us whole years to mend Arvelia's magic. And we always believed Korvel was dead.
Today I am not sure. Perhaps his soul is held in the walls…
…in remnants of old spells that never quite vanished…
…waiting to take revenge and to rule the castle again. I do not know. But it may be.
Nobody says anything.
Then you, {wizard}, have beaten him once already.
So it is. Love is the most powerful magic.
Keep those who love you always near, and give them back their love.
Only so will you reach all that you can be.
And go in peace: I know of it now.
Most likely, if anything was left of Korvel, it vanished when the threads were broken.
But we shall stay watchful, ready in case he strikes again.
It is the end-of-year dinner. Zarek sits beside Rinlo, grumbling: "Orla has told me to help you with the broom… I think I can do it."
Orla names the three of you pupils of Arvelia in your own right. The second year awaits.
"You began by taking a step, trying to get through a door, and you have found true friendship."
Over the year you learned to give orders with their arguments, to cast spells and carry things, to keep values with a name and read what things know of themselves…
…to count cells, to wait and to choose with `if` and `else`, to repeat with `for` and `while`, to use lists, to fly, to write functions of your own with `def`…
…and at last classes, objects, `__init__`, inheriting and methods.
But, above all, you learned the worth of friendship, and that the most powerful magic is love.
Until next year.
